page: Microsoft Azure FX16mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at a base frequency of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 336.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 21.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also perform strongly, ranking in the top 25%. However, the Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 25%, indicating a potential bottleneck in specific memory-intensive operations despite the large capacity. Multi-core performance, static web serving, and Redis SET operations remain in the average tier.

Given its high memory density and dedicated high-frequency Intel Xeon processor, this instance offers a specialized hardware profile where resource density justifies the cost for memory-bound workloads. It is designed for memory-intensive databases, large-scale caching layers, and enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM without requiring a massive vCPU count. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets like AMX and AVX-512 also makes it capable of handling localized machine learning inference and cryptographic workloads.
